name: Yves Tumor
label: Warp
lede: A Miami-born, Knoxville-raised kid who toured Europe and Asia with Mykki Blanco, cut a record for PAN, then turned up on Warp sounding like Prince with a noise pedalboard.

eras.title: Knoxville escape, Mykki's road
eras.text: Sean Lee Bowie grew up in Tennessee, left, and ended up in Los Angeles making post-chillwave as T.E.A.M.S. A two-and-a-half-year tour with Mykki Blanco took the project through Europe and Asia.

years.h: Sean Lee Bowie is born in Miami
years.p: Raised in Knoxville, Tennessee, he starts making music in his mid-teens as a way out of what he calls dull, conservative surroundings.
years.xp:
Wikipedia has Bowie born in Miami on November 19, 1989, and raised in Knoxville, where he taught himself drums, bass, guitar and keyboards. It says he began making music at 16; a 2019 profile in Something Curated says 17.

He left Tennessee at 20, moving to San Diego and then Los Angeles after college. The name he records under, Yves Tumor, came later; before it, he worked as T.E.A.M.S.

years.cap: Performer Yves Tumor playing a show in 2019 · Wikimedia
years.h: Mykki Blanco takes him on the road for two and a half years
years.p: The two meet in Los Angeles in 2012, and the collaboration becomes a Europe-and-Asia tour run.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and Something Curated both date the meeting to 2012, and both say the touring lasted about two and a half years. By then Bowie was still recording as T.E.A.M.S., which AllMusic described as post-chillwave.

Tumor appears on four tracks of Blanco's Mykki Blanco Presents C-ORE (2015): "Histrionic I," "Childish," "Histrionic II" and "Histrionic III / Skunk of the Earth."

years.h: T.E.A.M.S. is retired
years.p: Bowie shelves the post-chillwave name and starts over as Yves Tumor.

eras.title: Self-released, then PAN, then Warp
eras.text: Three records in three set-ups: a self-released cassette, a debut on Berlin's PAN, and a compilation that doubled as the news that Warp had signed him.

years.h: When Man Fails You goes out on cassette and download
years.p: His first release as Yves Tumor is self-released, and Apothecary Compositions reissues it on April 29, 2016.

years.src: Wikipedia: Serpent Music · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: Serpent Music: the PAN debut, three years in the making
years.p: Recorded across Miami, Leipzig, Los Angeles and Berlin. Pitchfork gave it 7.3 and Noisey ranked it No. 13 of 2016.
years.xp:
He had been calling the record "God Fearing" and kept it off Bandcamp so it wouldn't leak. After PAN founder Bill Kouligas praised the unfinished record, Tumor finished it for release. Wikipedia lists both September 22 and 23 for the date.

Metacritic scores it 77 from six reviews, and Pitchfork's Andy Beta compared the looped, field-recorded mood to James Ferraro and Dean Blunt.

years.big: "I never thought of it as soul music."
q: I never thought of it as soul music, but that's just what I was doing.
years.h: Soul music, by accident
years.p: Tumor's own take on Serpent Music, whose seed was the Motown and soul records his father played in the house.
years.xp: Tumor told interviewers the record drew on personal relationships, spiritual themes and the music his father played when he was young. The finished album mixes soul, ambient, club, psychedelia and noise.

years.h: Experiencing the Deposit of Faith arrives with the Warp news
years.p: The self-released compilation drops the same day Warp Records announces it has signed him.

eras.title: Safe in the Hands of Warp
eras.text: The first Warp record was announced three days before it existed in full, and it made Tumor a name critics argued over for a year.

years.h: "Noid" is the first Warp single, with a police-violence video
years.p: Andreas Brauning's video follows Tumor through downtown Los Angeles and into police abuse; Rolling Stone called it a jarring examination of the police state.

years.cap: Safe in the Hands of Love, Warp, 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Safe in the Hands of Love · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: Safe in the Hands of Love appears with no warning
years.p: Three singles, a September 4 track from Warp, and then the whole album on September 5. Pitchfork gave it 9.1.
years.xp:
It was recorded at Paulie Sphere Sound in Mount Washington, Los Angeles, with Justin Raisen co-producing. The singles were "Noid" (July 24), "Licking an Orchid" with James K (August 29) and "Lifetime" (September 3).

Pitchfork's Jayson Greene wrote that it "dwarfs everything the artist has released by several orders of magnitude." Metacritic scores it 89; the CD and LP followed on October 12.

years.h: A live band forms: Rothman, Hastings, Greatti, Ramirez
years.p: Yves Rothman (keys, musical director), Rhys Hastings (drums), Chris Greatti (lead guitar) and Gina Ramirez (bass) become Tumor's touring and recording group.

years.h: All Points East, London
years.p: Something Curated lists Tumor at the London festival on this date, in the wake of the Warp record.

years.h: Safe in the Hands of Love wins a Libera Award
years.p: At the 2019 Libera Awards it took Best Dance/Electronic Record, and was also nominated for Record of the Year and Best Outlier Record.

eras.title: Guitars, pandemic, and a Prince problem
eras.text: Heaven to a Tortured Mind came out in the first month of lockdown and was written about as glam-rock and psychedelic soul. The EP a year later went for shoegaze.

years.src: Wikipedia: Heaven to a Tortured Mind · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: Heaven to a Tortured Mind: guitars, swagger, No. 7 of 2020 at Pitchfork
years.p: Justin Raisen and Mahssa Taghinia produce with Tumor. Metacritic scores it 88 from 18 reviews.
years.xp:
Singles were "Gospel for a New Century" (February 18), "Kerosene!" featuring Diana Gordon, and "Romanticist / Dream Palette" (March 19). The Guardian's Alexis Petridis made it Album of the Week, and Wikipedia notes comparisons to Prince and David Bowie.

Pitchfork's Kevin Lozano called it "a gratifying and intense record, one whose pleasures are viscerally immediate."

years.h: Lockdown: furniture, upholstery, and welding plans
years.p: During the pandemic Tumor designed furniture, got into upholstery and architecture, and said he planned to move into welding construction.

years.h: Guest spots: Joji's "Reanimator" and a four-way jam
years.p: He features on "Reanimator" from Joji's Nectar, and on "Let All the Poisons That Lurk in the Mud Seep Out" with Kelsey Lu, Kelly Moran and Moses Boyd.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Asymptotical World · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: The Asymptotical World EP: shoegaze, nu-metal, goth
years.p: Tumor, Yves Rothman and new guitarist Chris Greatti share the instruments; Pitchfork gave it 7.8 and Loud and Quiet 9.
years.xp: The lead single "Jackie" came out June 15, 2021, and got compared to A.R. Kane and My Bloody Valentine. The video was nominated for a Video of the Year award in 2022. The EP wrote all tracks but "Tuck," which has lyrics co-written with Agnes Gryczkowska.

eras.title: Hot between worlds
eras.text: A year on the road, a Willow feature, then the album Pitchfork placed at No. 31. It's the loudest, tightest record in the catalogue, with the live band inside it.

years.h: World tour with October and the Eyes, Timkoh and Doss
years.p: Tumor tours internationally through 2022; the Willow collaboration "Perfectly Not Close to Me" arrives from her album Coping Mechanism.

years.h: "God Is a Circle" announces the next record
years.p: The first single from the coming Warp album, released with a dark video covered by NME.

yt: "Heaven Surrounds Us Like a Hood" official video
years.h: "Heaven Surrounds Us Like a Hood" gets a psychedelic video
years.p: The third single from the album, covered by The FADER and DIY.

years.src: Wikipedia: Praise a Lord · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: Praise a Lord Who Chews...: Pitchfork 8.4, No. 31 of 2023
years.p: Pitchfork's Jayson Greene gave it 8.4 and ranked it No. 31 of 2023. Metacritic scores it 86 from 19 critics.
years.xp:
Produced by Tumor with Noah Goldstein, Simon Christensen, Elliott Kozel and Dylan Wiggins, the fifth album runs 37 minutes. The singles were "God Is a Circle," "Echolalia" (January 30), "Heaven Surrounds Us Like a Hood" and "Parody" (March 15).

Year-end lists put it No. 1 at Consequence, No. 4 at Vulture, No. 16 at The Guardian and No. 32 at Stereogum.
play: Praise a Lord Who Chews but Which Does Not Consume; (Or Simply, Hot Between Worlds)

years.h: Kanye West's Sunday Service choir sings on "Parody"
years.p: NPR notes the Samples, the choir from West's Sunday Service, provide the vocals.

years.big: A record about being watched, and about looking back
q: It gives me life when something is made that no one saw happening.
years.h: What gives him life
years.p: NPR's review reads the album as private identity against public persona, dressed in pop language from Motown to Prince.
years.xp: The NPR review says the record opens with a scream and ends on an invitation to lock eyes. It also notes Tumor told artist Kembra Pfahler: "I like to go on hikes and I like swimming."

years.h: To Spite or Not to Spite Tour starts in Indio and ends in Dublin
years.p: Dates run April 4 to November 27, 2023, with Pretty Sick, Frost Children, Izzy Spears, Evanora Unlimited and Nation opening.

eras.title: Lineup turns and a bad summer
eras.text: The band changes guitarists, Tumor drops a SoundCloud mixtape, and works with Rosalía and Björk. In August 2026 the press reports allegations against him.

years.h: Maro Chon replaces Greatti on lead guitar
years.p: Wikipedia lists Greatti and Ramirez as 2019 to 2024 members and Maro Chon as the lead guitarist from 2024.

years.h: American Idol - The Greatest Notes Chapter 1 on SoundCloud
years.p: A 2024 mixtape released on SoundCloud, off the Warp schedule.

years.h: Rosalía's "Berghain," with Björk
years.p: Tumor appears on "Berghain" from Rosalía's Lux, alongside Björk, and on a track with Nina called "We Don't Count."

years.h: Multiple women accuse Tumor of assault; he denies it
years.p: Stereogum and others report the allegations, including video from musician Angel Money; Tumor called them "100% untrue" and vowed legal action.
years.xp:
Stereogum reports an anonymous post on the Yves Tumor subreddit, Angel Money's video from a record-release party, and a statement from collaborator Kidä describing the experience in his touring band as "one of the most disrespectful professional experiences". The FADER and NME covered the accusations.

Tumor responded on Instagram, then in a follow-up called them "completely disgusting, salacious lies" from someone he barely knew. Stereogum's article mentions upcoming Bumbershoot dates but gives no cancellations or label response.
